# Lighting upgrades for off-road visibility

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Mount light bar or individual spotlights in locations such as roof, hood, front bumper mouth, or headlight slots. [t1031]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Select a light bar or individual spotlights based on budget and desired beam pattern.
2. Mount the lights in locations such as the roof, hood, front bumper mouth, or headlight slots.

_Procedure reported by [t1031]._

## Parts

- [Partial] B&M Light Bar: Homebrew option from Xterra Performance [t1031]
- [Partial] Eagle Eye Lights, 6" or 7": Available as individual units or sets of four [t1031]
- HID Fog Lamps, 7": Self-contained housing, sold in pairs for ~$100 [t1031]
- KC Daylighters, 6": 130W long range with yellow covers and rock guards available separately [t1031]
- [Partial] N.Y.X LED Light Bars: Suggested for cheap 22-inch bars [t1031]

## Tips & gotchas

- Combine individual lights with a homebrew or B&M bar to keep costs around $200. [t1031]
- [Partial] Consider low-end LED bars if budget allows more than standard halogens. [t1031]
- [Partial] Mounting 32-inch bars above the windshield, on the hood, or in the bumper mouth requires minimal work. [t1031]

## Common mistakes

- Placing lights too close to a CB antenna may cause radio interference unless adjusted. [t1031]
